subject: Clarifications on model provenance, version-pinning, and license compatibility
body:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI follow-up: model catalog provenance + pinning questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our RFI we need a concise set of responses on three specific points in the model catalog section: provenance mapping for each open model, policy and support for version pinning (how to pin to a specific model binary + rollback), and the licensing compatibility matrix for derived models. Our security and procurement teams want the answers inline to our checklist below so we can move to draft terms next week.

Quick checklist (we'll copy into the RFI doc):
- For each model in your public catalog, provide a provenance chain (origins, training data provenance summary, and any known third-party components).
- Does Redwood support immutable model pins (model hash + version) for serving? If yes, how are updates rolled out and how do you handle automatic fallback to pinned versions?
- Provide a matrix of open-source licenses you accept (e.g., Apache-2.0, MIT, CC-BY-SA, etc.) and whether derivatives or commercial use are allowed under your hosted service.
- Any known flagged licenses or encumbrances we should be aware of?

Can you send a one-page summary per bullet and a brief technical appendix? Also please include any artifacts (signed attestations, internal provenance exporter, or SOC2 summary) that expedite our security reviews.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager, Globex

-----Original Message-----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@globex.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: model catalog provenance + pinning questions

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear checklist; appreciate the structure. Attaching a concise package that maps to those bullets and a short technical appendix for your engineering/security teams. Highlights below:

1) Provenance mapping
- We publish a model-catalog manifest per model that includes model origin (source checkpoint + upstream owner when applicable), tokenizer/fairseq/transformers versions, and a short note on public datasets used in pretraining/fine-tuning where permitted. See appendix sheet tab "Provenance" (attached).
- Where upstream model authors have provided provenance manifests (e.g., license headers, model card), we preserve and surface those verbatim. For community-contributed variants we record the contributor and link to the originating repo.

2) Version pinning and rollout
- We support immutable pins: each served artifact is associated with a content-addressable model id (model_hash:vX). Customers can specify model_id pinned at the route or deployment level.
- Rolling updates are controlled by rollout policies: canary -> linear -> full, or immediate. We provide automatic fallback to the last known-good pinned model on detection of runtime errors or quality regressions.
- We also expose a "pin-lock" control in Redwood Private so on-prem deployments can disable automatic updates entirely.

3) License compatibility matrix
- Attached: a compatibility matrix (tab "Licenses") describing which open-source licenses we accept as upstream, and the conditions for commercial use under our hosted API. Short summary: Apache-2.0 and MIT are accepted without restriction for hosting and derivative work in hosted service; GPL-family licenses are flagged and require escalated legal review for hosting/derivative distribution. CC-BY-SA is conditionally allowed depending on downstream obligations — see matrix.

Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Model-Catalog_Appendix.pdf (2 pages), provenance-mapping-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-model rows), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 control summary).

I'll paste the appendix highlights below for quick copy into your RFI. Marcus and Aditya are on the thread for any architecture or commercial questions.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 26 Nov 2026 at 10:05 AM, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:

Hi Laura / Kimberly —

Quick technical clarifications that may be helpful for your security team to include verbatim:

- Model IDs: we compute a SHA256 over the serialized weights + tokenizer config to generate model_hash. That hash is included in the model manifest and visible in the catalog API.
- Provenance exporter: an opt-in pipeline (open-source) exports provenance metadata as a JSON-LD manifest that can be ingested into customers' asset inventory. We can provide an example output for any catalog model.
- Runtime safety and rollback: our serving runtime monitors per-request error rates and perplexity drift vs. a configured baseline; thresholds can trigger automated rollback to pinned model IDs or to a secondary model family.

If you want, we can provide a small example manifest and the exporter output for one of the catalog models (attaching a sample row in the provenance sheet).

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal SE, Redwood Inference

On Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800, Jacob Mills <jmills@globex.com> wrote:

Thanks Kimberly / Marcus — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our security folks:

1) Can you confirm which licenses you consider "disallowed" for hosted commercial inference? We need an explicit list to run with our legal team.
2) Can you provide a signed attestation that the provenance exporter is run prior to any production push for models in the Redwood public catalog? If not signed, please provide a process doc naming roles and checkpoints.
3) Please add a short SOC2 summary called out in the RFI (controls relevant to model artifact integrity and change control).

Would appreciate these by EOD Monday if possible.

Jacob Mills
Director, IT Security — Globex

On Mon, 29 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:

Jacob / Laura / Kimberly —

Looping in Grace for legal clarifications. Attached is a one-page license policy excerpt we provide to prospects and a proposed attestation template. Highlights:
- Disallowed (for hosting/derivative distribution): AGPL-3.0, GPL-3.0 (unless accompanied by a commercial grant), any model that includes non-redistributable third-party components.
- Conditionally allowed with restrictions: CC-BY-SA (requires downstream compliance with share-alike obligations; we recommend self-hosting for datasets/models under that license).
- Accepted without restriction for hosting: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2/3.

Attestation: we can provide a signed attestation for Globex covering catalog models as part of the procurement pack. Our SOC2 summary (attached earlier) includes change control and artifact integrity controls; I pulled the most relevant control IDs into the attestation template.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to provide signed attestation + license matrix doc (by COB tomorrow).
- Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive with Marcus and Grace for Wed morning (Nov 30).
- If all good, procurement to share draft SOW / draft DPA and we will confirm pricing/terms.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
